doc.name: A — lounge furniture catalogue, grid of cubes, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: bouclé lounge chair
Category: lounge furniture
Shot programme: grid of cubes
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the art director signing off every frame of this lounge furniture campaign. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the low-angle monument in a grid of cubes treatment.

SUBJECT. A bouclé lounge chair. Lock the product itself to the reference — no proportional drift, no invented branding, no cleaned-up typography. Everything else in the frame is your design decision.

CAMERA. Low angle looking up so the product reads as architecture against the backdrop. Shoot on a 58mm vintage double-gauss at f/4, framing for a tight crop that breaks the subject at the frame edge.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with underlighting from a translucent base panel. Stage the product on or against mirrored steel, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a neutral commercial grade with clean whites and no colour cast. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
